itinerary.cal: Best attempted in late summer (Aug-Sep) once the glacier crossing between Tin Can Gap and the Middle/North col is more consolidated and less crevassed; carry a rope, rack, and glacier gear in addition to standard scrambling kit.

days.note: Same approach as the standard South Peak trip: Saddle Lake Trailhead through old-growth forest and Saddle Lake up to the meadows at Goat Flats. Carry the technical rack and glacier gear in addition to overnight kit since North Peak's harder climbing is ahead.
days.title: Hike in to Goat Flats camp

days.note: From camp, cross Tin Can Gap and drop roughly 400 ft onto the Queest-Alb Glacier before climbing back up about 1,000 ft to the col between Middle and North Peak. Rope up for sustained class 4 climbing with one low-5th-class (5.1) move in a summit chimney; exposure is constant.
days.title: Technical summit day: North Peak

schedule.label: Leave Goat Flats camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start to cross the glacier while snow is firm.

schedule.label: Reach Tin Can Gap, descend to the glacier
schedule.detail: Steep snow down to the Queest-Alb Glacier.

schedule.label: Cross glacier, climb to the Middle/North col
schedule.detail: ~1,000 ft regain; watch for crevasses late season.

schedule.label: Rope up for the rock
schedule.detail: Class 4 to low 5th class (5.1), one exposed chimney move.

schedule.label: Summit North Peak
schedule.detail: 6,870 ft, highest of the three fingers.

days.objective: Climb North Peak via the Queest-Alb Glacier and the Middle/North col

days.note: Break camp at Goat Flats and retrace the trail down through Saddle Lake to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip: hike in to Goat Flats, a long technical day crossing the Queest-Alb Glacier and climbing class 4 to low-5th-class (5.1) rock to North Peak, then hike out; roughly 14.5 mi and 5,400 ft of cumulative gain overall.

itinerary.cal: Beta is thin for this specific summit -- confirm current glacier/snow conditions on the Queest-Alb crossing before committing, and plan for a rope and light rack even though the South Face itself is mostly 3rd/4th class.

days.note: Same shared approach as the other Three Fingers summits: Saddle Lake Trailhead up through old-growth forest and Saddle Lake to the meadows at Goat Flats.
days.title: Hike in to Goat Flats camp

days.note: From camp, traverse via Tin Can Gap toward the saddle between Middle and North Peak, then climb Middle Peak's South Face -- steep snow/scree giving way to class 3-4 rock, with a rope useful for the short exposed moves near the summit ridge.
days.title: Technical summit day: Middle Peak South Face
days.objective: Climb Middle Peak via the saddle and South Face

days.note: Break camp at Goat Flats and retrace the trail down through Saddle Lake to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip shaped like the North Peak itinerary: hike in to Goat Flats, a technical South Face summit day via the Middle/North col, then hike out; roughly 14.5 mi and an estimated 5,100 ft of cumulative gain overall.

access.fees: $5 day-use Northwest Forest Pass (or annual pass) at the trailhead
access.notes: None required for day use; Northwest Forest Pass recommended for parking. Digital Recreation Day Pass available via Recreation.gov for Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest day-use sites. Overnight use requires separate permits; verify current conditions with Verlot Public Service Center (360) 691-7791. Tupso Pass Road (FS 41) washed out 4.8 miles in (past Canyon Creek bridge at mile 8); permanently closed to vehicles. Hiking and biking allowed. Approximately 9 additional miles to actual trailhead required - bicycle recommended for approach.
access.rules: Boulder River Wilderness: group size limited to 12; no campfires within 1/4 mile of Trail #641 from Saddle Lake or in the Goat Flats area; no camping within 200 ft of Saddle/Bandana Lake shorelines; Leave No Trace
access.permit: None required — free self-issue wilderness permits available at trailheads/ranger stations for day/overnight travel where the peak is inside designated wilderness.
access.closures: Tupso Pass Road (FR 41) washed out ~4.8 miles in and closed to vehicles beyond the Canyon Creek bridge (~mile 8.5) since 2023 — check current MBS NF alerts before driving out

road.name: Tupso Pass Road (FR 41)
road.status: Washed out at approximately mile 4.8; permanently closed to vehicle travel beyond the Canyon Creek bridge (~mile 8.5)

days.note: The hardest of Vesper's North Face testpieces, starting just left of True Grit and following bolted friction slabs and a long seam pitch. Same approach as the other North Face routes (Sunrise Mine Trailhead to Vesper Lake, then a short scramble to the base) and the same Class 2 talus walk-off.
days.title: Fish & Whistle, car to car

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Earlier start recommended given the harder, slower pitches.

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Base is ~50 ft left of the True Grit start.

schedule.label: Top out
schedule.detail: 5 pitches, cruxes on P1/P3/P5 (5.9-5.10-), P1/2 and P3/4 link with a 60m rope.

schedule.label: Descend
schedule.detail: Class 2 southeast talus gully back to Vesper Lake.

days.objective: Climb Fish & Whistle (5.10-, 5 pitches) on Vesper's North Face

itinerary.totalNote: A long, harder single day car-to-car: ~11-12 hrs, ~4,400 ft gain, 5 pitches up to 5.10-.

days.note: The Ragged Edge day plan: a long single push from the Sunrise Mine Trailhead through Headlee Pass to Vesper Lake, up 6 pitches of low-angle slab/corner climbing on the North Face, then a Class 2 talus walk-off back to the lake and out.

pro_tips: Target February-April, ideally right after a low-elevation snowstorm and a solid refreeze, for the firmest, most predictable conditions
Stash skis or other snow-travel gear around 2,500 ft in the old growth on the way up to lighten the bushwhack, and retrieve it on descent
Start pre-dawn — the entire route is exposed to avalanche and wet-slide danger once the sun hits it

itinerary.cal: Best done Feb-April in a high-pressure window after a refreeze; brushy/rocky lower gulch and rime-plastered cirque are far safer when snow-covered and consolidated.

days.note: Also a single-day push, not an overnight trip: an early start up Snow Gulch and a steep timbered/rocky ridge (stashing non-essential gear partway), then skinning or booting a glacier basin below the summit block and climbing a short, steep (~50 deg) final pitch. Real ski-descent and climbing trip reports show ~12 hours car-to-car for a fit party in good spring conditions.
days.title: Car-to-car via Snow Gulch and the NW Face

schedule.label: Leave trailhead / Moose Creek barricade
schedule.detail: Pre-dawn start; drive/walk to the Snow Gulch approach.

schedule.label: Reach Snow Gulch
schedule.detail: Old forest road/creek approach; can be icy and slippery low down.

schedule.label: Top of the bushwhack ridge (~2,500-3,600 ft)
schedule.detail: Stash non-essential gear near 2,500 ft; boots/crampons on the ridge, skis or foot travel above as snow softens.

schedule.label: Reach the glacier basin below the summit block
schedule.detail: Steep rock walls plastered with rime line the cirque.

schedule.label: Climb the final ~50 deg pitch to the summit
schedule.detail: Short but genuinely steep icy snow; axe and second tool/whippet recommended.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Descend the same line before the snowpack warms further; upper snow can turn to breakable crust by afternoon.

days.objective: Climb the Northwest Face ice/snow line to the summit and descend same day

itinerary.totalNote: A demanding single day: about 6,400 ft gain over ~13 mi round trip, roughly 12 hours car-to-car in a good spring refreeze window.

climate.typical: Wet, maritime west-slope Cascades climate with well over 100 in/yr precipitation; the prime window for this route is a stable high-pressure period after a refreeze, not just a calendar season.

bySeason.fall: Not a typical season for this line
bySeason.spring: Prime season (Feb-April) — deep snow covers the brush and buries the approach, but the entire uptrack is avalanche terrain; go right after a storm cycle refreezes
bySeason.summer: Route becomes the standard Northwest Shoulder summer scramble as snow recedes and the glacier opens crevasses
bySeason.winter: Occasionally skied/climbed in deep-snow years but avalanche hazard is severe and daylight short

road.name: 387th Ave NE / Old Mine Road (unsigned FS spur off SR-530)
road.status: Paved for about the first 0.5 mile off SR-530, then gravel; dead-ends at the boulder-and-steel-gate barricade where the Moose Creek bridge was removed in 2008.
road.driveNote: From Darrington go ~5 mi west on SR-530 (from Arlington ~26 mi east) to the Whitehorse store at Mine Road, turn south, and follow the gravel spur ~0.6-0.75 mi to the barricade.
road.seasonalGate: No formal gate, but access is frequently snowed-in during this route's prime Feb-April season — check current conditions.
